browser_validation.evidence_reason: The verified browser workflow or one of its jobs did not conclude successfully.
browser_validation.accessibility_scope: Prepared browser checks cover form labels, keyboard focus, and primary control names; they do not establish WCAG conformance or screen-reader behavior.
browser_validation.evidence_artifact: GitHub Actions workflow run and completed job conclusions

incomplete_in_scope_features: Data transparency and deployment-specific privacy terms
mandatory_evidence_not_passed: Human acceptance MVP-01 through MVP-12 on a real browser/device
Real-browser mobile visual, overflow, keyboard, and accessibility behavior
Site-specific privacy terms, operator contact, retention, and deletion process
Live HTTPS deployment, provider PHP/extensions, session cookie, filesystem permissions, and routes

EVIDENCE: Production home route and learner entry links are exercised by LearnerJourneyHttpTest.

Batch 663 production HTTP fixture traverses board detail, effective subject link, study library, eligible practice, answer, explanation, result, history, progress, retry, and stale-action recovery for all ten boards.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Practice quiz lifecycle, question selection, answers, explanations, submission, results, and recovery
EVIDENCE: HTTP journey tests exercise production route handling, answer feedback, result review, exact-once persistence, stale submissions, and restart behavior.
Historical result retrieval rejects records owned by a different anonymous learner identity.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Dashboard, progress, weakness analysis, and adaptive recommendations
EVIDENCE: Learner-facing aggregates and recommendations are tied to the current session identity. Batch 665 keeps subject/topic performance, weakness recommendations, study-plan actions, and result retries scoped to the recorded board and LET/CSE exam variant; the ten-board production HTTP test follows the retry action rendered on each result page.

BoardPrep provides a configurable study simulation with timed and untimed sessions, a persisted server deadline, refresh recovery, previous/skip/jump navigation, editable answers, required review before manual submission, automatic expiration, unanswered scoring, and exact-once result persistence. The interface identifies the simulator as separate from the official examination and does not claim official timing or format.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Official exam-format fidelity and published duration for every board
EVIDENCE: Timer duration is learner-configured for study use. Board-specific official formats and durations require current authoritative examination sources and are not represented as official.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Flashcard discovery, reveal, review, and scheduling
EVIDENCE: HTTP tests cover reveal-before-rating, CSRF-protected review, storage, filters, empty states, and learner ownership.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Source-backed study library and flashcard-to-material navigation
EVIDENCE: Published materials include provenance; Batch 662 verifies board-scoped discovery and direct material links from flashcard references.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Question-level study support in practice feedback and result review
EVIDENCE: All 8,962 canonical questions have study-question links in the baseline data; Batch 662 renders the linked published material from feedback and result review.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Anonymous learner identity and same-browser persistence
EVIDENCE: Random per-session learner identities scope attempts, weakness, and flashcard state; cookie clearing loses access to that identity.

Current-commit desktop/mobile Chromium evidence verifies responsive layouts at five target widths, keyboard navigation, browser accessibility semantics, privacy controls, and all ten board journeys. Automation does not establish screen-reader behavior or WCAG conformance; all twelve owner human acceptance cases remain separate.
MVP_RELEASE_SCOPE.md excludes role-based production administration; curated content is release-managed. Developer authoring and Doctor routes are disabled in production.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Production error handling and private diagnostics boundary
EVIDENCE: Production mode suppresses detailed exception output and rejects Developer/Doctor HTTP routes; health output is intentionally limited.

feature_assessment.FEATURE: Data transparency and deployment-specific privacy terms
EVIDENCE: Batch 663 provides session-scoped saved-data counts, a privacy export, and CSRF/confirmation-protected deletion with session rotation. Deployment owner identity, contact, approved retention, hosting logs, and backup practices remain unsupplied.

findings.USER_IMPACT: A learner following a study-support title could not reach the referenced material directly.
findings.EVIDENCE: FlashcardDerivationService supplied material_id, but the review template linked every reference to /study-library.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Open a revealed flashcard with study references and activate a reference title.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The learner template discarded the material identity already present in derived references.

findings.USER_IMPACT: Learners on an examination detail page had no direct way to open the material library filtered to that board.
findings.EVIDENCE: home/exam.php linked to practice and exam mode but had no study-library link; StudyLibraryService already supports board filtering.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Open /exams?exam=LET and inspect the board actions.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The board detail template did not connect its available study-material route.

findings.USER_IMPACT: Every page displayed an obsolete v0.1 footer on the v1.0.1 product.
findings.EVIDENCE: The shared layout contained a literal BoardPrep v0.1 label.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Open any production learner page and inspect the footer.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The footer version was hard-coded and not connected to release configuration.

findings.USER_IMPACT: Learners had no in-product explanation that progress is tied to a browser session and remains server-side after cookie clearing.
findings.EVIDENCE: No privacy/data handling route or notice was present in the production route table or shared navigation.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Review production navigation and footer before Batch 662.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The release documented session settings but did not disclose learner-state behavior to learners.
DEPENDENCIES: Site-specific privacy terms remain an open launch capability.

findings.USER_IMPACT: A learner could mistake exam mode for a timed, exact official exam replica.
findings.EVIDENCE: The learner-configured timer, answer withholding, question navigation, review gate, and unanswered results are covered by Batch 670 tests. Official duration and format fidelity remain deferred, and the interface identifies this as a separate study simulator.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Open quiz setup, select Exam Simulation, and inspect the setup instructions and session behavior.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The mode's supported limits were not disclosed at its point of use.
DEPENDENCIES: Current authoritative official format and duration evidence for every board remains deferred.

findings.USER_IMPACT: Learners could read a question explanation but could not follow its linked source-backed material from practice feedback or result review.
findings.EVIDENCE: All 8,962 canonical questions have entries in study-question-links.json; quiz views did not render those links before Batch 662.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Submit an answer or open a historical result for a linked question and look for a study-support link.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: Question-to-material mappings were used by data validation and flashcard derivation but not connected to learner quiz templates.

findings.USER_IMPACT: A valid source registry was reported invalid by the existing source/study regression check, obscuring genuine provenance defects and making the test suite fail.
findings.EVIDENCE: The committed sources.json uses 11 additional source_type categories that SourceRegistryService::validate() did not accept.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Run php tools/Tests/SourceStudyLibraryTest.php against the Batch 661 baseline.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The validator's hard-coded allowed-type list was not updated with the committed source taxonomy.

findings.USER_IMPACT: Practice entry points for seven board codes could lead to an empty question pool even though the selected board had eligible questions.
findings.EVIDENCE: QuestionEligibilityService and QuestionEligibilityIndex normalized LET/CSE aliases only; direct checks found no match for CLE, NLE, PLE, CE, ME, REE, or ARCH against their configured board IDs. TenBoardLearnerJourneyHttpTest now exercises each public code through production HTTP.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Start /quiz with exam=CLE, NLE, PLE, CE, ME, REE, or ARCH and a board-eligible subject; before the fix selection returned no eligible question.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: Board short codes were not normalized to the canonical board IDs used by eligibility records.

findings.FEATURE: Effective board subjects and practice setup
findings.USER_IMPACT: Board detail pages could omit available subjects, and practice settings exposed only LET/CSE subject options, making direct focused practice inaccessible or misleading for other boards.
findings.EVIDENCE: home/exam.php rendered configured board-subject relations and linked subject codes, while runtime eligibility resolves effective blueprint subjects. Quiz settings contained hard-coded English/CSE options. TenBoardLearnerJourneyHttpTest verifies displayed effective subjects lead to an eligible question and complete results for every board.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Open /exams?exam=CPA or another board and follow a displayed subject into practice; before the fix, the page could show no usable subject action or submit a nonmatching subject.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The board detail and quiz setup UI were not built from the same effective subject IDs used by question eligibility and selection.

findings.USER_IMPACT: The owner preview and browser test server could not start from the committed application archive, blocking local acceptance preparation.
findings.EVIDENCE: The committed archive measured 103,260,160 bytes, exceeding spawnSync's default 64 MiB output buffer; file-backed archive extraction now starts the production fixture and serves safe routes.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Run node tests/browser/server.cjs on the Batch 663 baseline; it failed with 'Unable to export committed browser fixture'.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The test server buffered the complete git archive in memory with a 64 MiB cap.
findings.TEST_COVERAGE: Post-commit isolated production fixture smoke: /, /exams, /quiz?exam=LET, /privacy, and /health.php returned 200; developer and private paths returned 404.

findings.USER_IMPACT: Browser checks could report a learner flow that depended on subjects or question counts the visible product form does not offer.
findings.EVIDENCE: The prior helper injected hidden subject options and a two-question count directly into the DOM. It now selects only enabled visible choices and the offered five-question minimum.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Inspect the old startQuiz helper's evaluate/add Option logic and run it with a subject absent from the rendered form or count=2.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: Test setup bypassed the production UI and fabricated controls instead of exercising learner-visible inputs.
findings.TEST_COVERAGE: Browser test helper rejects unavailable visible options; production HTML options were checked over isolated HTTP. Playwright execution remains NOT_VERIFIED on Termux.
DEPENDENCIES: Run npm run test:browser on supported desktop or CI Chromium before browser evidence can pass.

findings.USER_IMPACT: The owner was instructed to start a three-question session even though the learner UI offers five as the minimum, making the acceptance case impossible as written.
findings.EVIDENCE: Quiz setup exposes a five-question minimum; the Android guide now specifies the smallest offered count and MVP-06 has a regression assertion.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Follow the prior Stage D/MVP-06 instructions and attempt to select three questions.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The human checklist assumed an unsupported question count rather than matching the real configuration options.
findings.TEST_COVERAGE: tools/Tests/ProductReadinessTest.php asserts the guide specifies five and no longer requests a three-question exam.

findings.USER_IMPACT: The product readiness report marked truthful learner-facing exam-mode limitations as undisclosed and incorrectly added a failed critical capability check.
findings.EVIDENCE: Setup and active-question pages state that BoardPrep exam simulations are separate from the official board examination. The readiness check verifies that boundary and the timer/review/expiry lifecycle regression.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Run php tools/product-readiness.php --json and inspect unsupported_exam_mode_claim_disclosed and exam_simulation_timer_review_and_expiry_regression.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: The readiness matcher accepted only one grammatical form and did not match the application's precise disclosure text.
findings.TEST_COVERAGE: tools/Tests/ProductReadinessTest.php asserts the live wording is recognized; the readiness output now reports the check PASS.

findings.USER_IMPACT: A learner retrying a completed engineering, health, accounting, architecture, or other non-CSE examination could be routed into LET practice instead of the board they just used.
findings.EVIDENCE: The Batch 665 baseline unit test reproduced result retry URLs without an exam parameter for all non-CSE boards. The production ten-board journey now extracts the rendered result action, validates its board, and starts the retry from that action.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Complete a practice attempt for a non-LET board and activate the primary retry action on its result page; before the fix, the generated URL omitted exam and QuizStartInputNormalizer defaulted to LET.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: QuizResultActionService only included board context for CSE/Civil Service even though completed sessions retain the board for every examination.

findings.FEATURE: Progress and adaptive recommendations merge boards and candidate variants
findings.USER_IMPACT: Scores for similarly named subjects and topics on different boards or candidate variants could be averaged together, and generated practice links could launch the wrong examination.
findings.EVIDENCE: The Batch 665 baseline analytics fixture combined CE/ME statics scores into one row and generated an unscoped recommendation. BoardScopedLearningContextTest now verifies board, LET level/specialization, and CSE level separation and validates generated action context.
findings.REPRODUCTION: Create attempts for CE and ME with the same subject/topic and different percentages; before the fix, topic analytics returned one blended row and its practice action defaulted to LET.
findings.ROOT_CAUSE: Topic and subject aggregation keys used only topic/subject, while recommendation, study-plan, and presentation paths dropped board and variant context.

missing_capabilities.FEATURE: Owner-approved deployment privacy terms and provider/log/backup disclosures
missing_capabilities.USER_IMPACT: Learners cannot yet identify the real site operator, contact channel, approved retention policy, or deployment-specific hosting/log/backup practices.
missing_capabilities.EVIDENCE: The privacy page supports owner-supplied environment configuration and clearly blocks public readiness when terms are absent. No real owner/provider values or approval were supplied for this batch.
missing_capabilities.REPRODUCTION: Open /privacy with no approved PRIVACY_* configuration; the application warns that public launch must wait for owner-approved terms.
missing_capabilities.ROOT_CAUSE: The application cannot invent legal/operator facts; the deployment owner and host must provide and approve these terms.
missing_capabilities.TEST_COVERAGE: tools/Tests/AnonymousLearnerPrivacyHttpTest.php verifies safe fail-closed disclosure; provider/legal approval remains unverified.
DEPENDENCIES: Real deployment owner and hosting contract

missing_capabilities.FEATURE: Session-scoped learner data export and deletion
missing_capabilities.USER_IMPACT: Without these controls, anonymous learners could neither inspect nor clear the application records tied to their current browser session.
missing_capabilities.EVIDENCE: Production privacy HTTP tests verify scoped export, CSRF and explicit confirmation, deletion of attempts/weakness/flashcard state, session rotation, idempotence, and preservation of another learner and aggregate statistics.
missing_capabilities.REPRODUCTION: Open /privacy, export the current session's records, then confirm a POST to /privacy/data/clear.
missing_capabilities.ROOT_CAUSE: The frozen release had disclosure only and no learner-facing data control route.
DEPENDENCIES: Owner-approved retention and hosting/log/backup terms remain tracked separately in BP662-CAP-001

missing_capabilities.USER_IMPACT: An anonymous learner cannot recover progress after switching browser/device or clearing the session cookie.
missing_capabilities.EVIDENCE: LearnerIdentityService stores a random ID in the PHP session; no account, login, password recovery, or identity linking routes exist. Cross-device access appears in long-term vision, not frozen MVP scope.
missing_capabilities.REPRODUCTION: Complete an attempt and open the app in a new browser session; learner history is not linked.
missing_capabilities.ROOT_CAUSE: The MVP intentionally uses anonymous browser-session identity.

missing_capabilities.FEATURE: Official exam-format fidelity and published duration for every board
missing_capabilities.USER_IMPACT: A learner could be misled if BoardPrep presented its generic study timer as an official board duration or implied that its question flow reproduces every board examination.
missing_capabilities.EVIDENCE: BoardPrep now offers a learner-configured timer and explicitly identifies the exam simulator as a study tool separate from the official examination. Current authoritative format and duration sources for every board have not been assembled.
missing_capabilities.REPRODUCTION: Review the exam simulation disclosure and compare its generic configurable timer with current official examination instructions for each board; no official duration or fidelity claim is made.
missing_capabilities.ROOT_CAUSE: The source corpus does not include verified current official exam-format and duration records for all boards.
DEPENDENCIES: Authoritative, current official format and duration evidence per board

missing_capabilities.USER_IMPACT: Operators cannot edit curated content from the public production UI.
missing_capabilities.EVIDENCE: All authoring and Doctor browser routes are registered only when APP_ENV is not production. MVP_RELEASE_SCOPE.md excludes role-based production administration.
missing_capabilities.REPRODUCTION: Request /developer or /question-editor in production; the routes are absent and return 404.
missing_capabilities.ROOT_CAUSE: Content is intended to change through reviewed code/release packages, not live web authoring.

configuration_controls: APP_ENV: production/development/testing; non-production enables Developer/Doctor HTTP routes
DB_DRIVER: json or sqlite in the production profile
DB_SQLITE_PATH: private SQLite file path when selected
APP_PUBLIC_PATH: CLI preflight document-root override; not an app feature flag
